title: --pids-limit and compat-API creates fail when no cgroup controller is delegated, even for unlimited
body:
On a WSL machine, where no cgroup controller is delegated, any request that sets a pids limit fails, including the two values that mean unlimited. Native `podman run` without the flag works, so `docker compose up -d` and any detached `docker run` cannot start a container while podman itself can.

```
$ podman machine ssh -- 'cat /proc/self/cgroup; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control'
0::/non-systemd/user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-c8.scope
          # subtree_control is empty: no controllers delegated

$ podman run --rm alpine true                   # ok
$ podman run -d --name a alpine sleep 3         # ok
$ docker run --rm alpine true                   # ok
$ docker run -d --name b alpine sleep 3         # fails
Error response from daemon: crun: controller `pids` is not available under /sys/fs/cgroup/non-systemd/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/<id>/cgroup.controllers: OCI runtime error

$ podman run --rm --pids-limit -1 alpine true   # fails, same error (-1 is unlimited)
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit 0 alpine true    # fails, same error (0 is unlimited)
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit 2048 alpine true # fails, same error
```

Cause: `PidsLimit()` in go.podman.io/common pkg/config/default.go returns 0 when rootless with a non-systemd cgroup manager and `InitResourceLimits` then sets no Pids resource, which is why the default path works; `GetResources` in pkg/specgenutil/specgen.go and the compat create handler in pkg/api/handlers/compat/containers.go set `ResourceLimits.Pids` whenever a value is given, and since 5fa0cb1090 the unlimited values normalize to -1, so crun still writes pids.max and needs the controller. Docker clients always send `PidsLimit: 0`, so every compat create hits it.

Suggested fix: omit the Pids resource when the normalized limit is unlimited, using the same rootless and cgroup-manager condition the default path already applies; a finite limit such as 2048 cannot be honoured here either, so a clear error would be better than the raw crun one.

Not reproducible on Linux: Ubuntu 26.04, rootless podman 5.7.0, cgroup_manager=systemd, `cpu memory pids` delegated to the user session. Everything above passes there, including `--cgroup-manager=cgroupfs -d`.

Workaround: `cgroups = "disabled"` in the machine's containers.conf, then `systemctl --user restart podman.socket`.

Related: #29749, #29874, #29826, #29883, 5fa0cb1090, podman-machine-os#319.
